mathematical_claims: T_cal has a classical model whose automorphism group contains a nontrivial involution fixing every prescribed finite tuple.
The model validates both iterator computations, coverage, separation, successor injectivity, identity iteration, body extensionality, and every numbering law I(n,k;u.Su)=S^k n for fixed standard k.
The model additionally validates every iterator fixed-point law and contextual induction for Boolean constant-target formulas.
As a further model property it validates induction for all first-order constant-target formulas; this stronger induction is not claimed derivable in iPRA.
With C(v,a,b)=I(v,a;w.b) and H(u)=S C(u,1,u), the literal equation I(Sn,0;u.H(u))=S(Sn) has derivable base and step but fails in the model.

T_cal is not ordinarily bi-interpretable with iPRA through finite parameters, finite-dimensional definable domains and quotient equalities when the interpretation and comparison parameters exist in the model; this includes provably inhabited parameter conditions.
proof_status: Written proof with independent mathematical review; not Lean/Rocq formalized.
novelty_scope: Relative to the pinned Chapter 10 question Parameters for the numbering theory. The existing T_cal obstruction covers standard parameters; the existing T_fus obstruction covers arbitrary finite parameters but fails N_0. New ingredient: three-label fibers and stabilizer-fixed equivariant path selection preserving all numbering laws while allowing independent chain flips.
